[Bug]: Anthropic→OpenAI conversion drops role on messages containing mcp_tool_use/mcp_tool_result blocks, causing 400 from all OpenAI-compatible providers
 #9721
New issue

Description
cuihairu
opened 
Description

When an Anthropic-protocol request (POST /anthropic/v1/messages) contains mcp_tool_use / mcp_tool_result content blocks in the message history, Bifrost's Anthropic → OpenAI conversion produces a message without a role field, causing every OpenAI-compatible upstream provider to reject the request with a 400.

deepseek/deepseek-flash → messages[0]: missing field \role``
sensenova/sensenova-6.8-flash-lite → field Messages[0].Role invalid, should be set
xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro → messages[7] role is not supported

Anthropic-native providers (e.g. zai, base_type anthropic) are unaffected since no conversion happens.

Standard tool_use / tool_result blocks convert correctly — only mcp_tool_* blocks trigger the bug.

Environment
Bifrost version: v2.4.0 (image maximhq/bifrost, sha256 a1c90607dcfd...)
Endpoint: POST /anthropic/v1/messages
Protocol: Anthropic Messages API (anthropic-version: 2023-06-01)
Minimal reproduction
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: $BIFROST_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash",
    "max_tokens": 30,
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
          {"type": "mcp_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1",
           "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "red"}]}
        ]
      },
      {"role": "user", "content": "reply OK"}
    ]
  }'

Actual response:

{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[0]: missing field `role` at line 1 column 56"}}

A fuller reproduction including the assistant-side block also fails:

"messages": [
  {"role": "user", "content": "look"},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": [
    {"type": "mcp_tool_use", "id": "call_1", "name": "analyze_image",
     "input": {"imageSource": "https://x/y.png", "prompt": "desc"},
     "server_name": "4_5v_mcp"}
  ]},
  {"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "mcp_tool_result", "tool_use_id": "call_1",
     "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "a red pixel"}]}
  ]},
  {"role": "user", "content": "reply OK"}
]
Expected behavior

Unknown / unsupported Anthropic content block types should be either:

dropped (ignored) during conversion, or
converted into a valid message (e.g. flattened into text content),

but the resulting OpenAI-format messages array must always contain a valid role on every entry. As a reference, LiteLLM handles the same request by stripping the unknown blocks and returns a normal 200.

Actual behavior

The converted messages array contains an entry with no role, so the upstream returns 400 for every OpenAI-compatible provider.

Impact

Claude Code (and similar Anthropic-protocol clients) persist tool-call history in conversation state. Sessions that previously used Z.ai's built-in MCP tools (e.g. analyze_image, which emits mcp_tool_use / mcp_tool_result blocks) cannot be routed to any OpenAI-compatible model after switching to Bifrost — every subsequent request fails with 400 until the old blocks are compacted out of history.

Additional context
Request logs show the 400 originates from the upstream provider, not from Bifrost's own validation.
Comparison: the identical request sent to LiteLLM's /v1/messages endpoint with an OpenAI-compatible backend succeeds (unknown blocks are dropped; input_tokens reflects stripped content).
